cycles_device: OPTIX: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU

phases.name: inspect
phases.what: damaged plug backed out 12 mm and turned 24 deg; wrench ready beside the cable, jaw axis already on the connector axis

phases.name: approach
phases.what: jaw moves level with the stub jacket behind the melted boot, its 34 mm opening facing the 17 mm cable

phases.name: hook
phases.what: jaw slides sideways onto the stub jacket at JawEntry

phases.name: slide
phases.what: jaw slides along the axis over boot and backshell onto the coupling nut (concentric, 1.5 mm radial clearance)

phases.name: grip
phases.what: jaw takes up the clearance; its rubber heel bears on the nut ridges (within 0.03 mm, measured on the meshes)

phases.name: seat
phases.what: wrench, nut and plug body move +12 mm along +Z; the cable follows through the Seated blend shape

phases.name: lock
phases.what: wrench and nut turn 24 deg clockwise as seen by the technician about the connector axis; marks line up

phases.name: release
phases.what: jaw centres again, clear of the nut

phases.name: back_off
phases.what: jaw slides back along the axis to JawExit on the seated stub jacket

phases.name: unhook
phases.what: jaw slides off the cable through its opening along the handle direction; tool clear

grip.meaning: the faceted jaw and nut first intersect 0.03 mm further in; the used offset leaves the rubber heel touching the ridges within that tolerance

f69_locked_pose_match.note: the damaged backshell was tessellated 24 deg turned; the plug body does not turn (keyed), so it is compared surface to surface

parts.note: all of these are joins inherited from the kit, hidden and unchanged by the motion: the cable end sits in the grommet hole and its start inside the torn jacket (both present at frame 0), and the kit models the coupling nut as a closed cylinder whose rear face sits inside the receptacle barrel once seated, exactly as in ConnectorRepaired. The wrench has no overlap with anything in any frame.
